trigger.raw_text: The Business Owner selects the Auction Customer RFM Report from the reporting options to analyze customer behavior using Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) metrics.

claims.content: The Business Owner selects the RFM Report from the Reports Menu.

The Auctions RFM Report provides RFM (Recency, Frequency, & Monetary) analysis to understand how the customer base is behaving and where to focus segmentation efforts based on the identification of the best customers in aggregate.
The Recency section is split into six tiers: 0-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, 91-180 days, 181-365 days, and over 365 days.
The Recency section shows the total number of accounts that have made a purchase transaction in each time range, as well as the revenue and orders amounts.

The grid cross-tabulates customer frequency (number of transactions on the account) against monetary value (total spend), with each cell showing accounts count, revenue, orders count, Rev / Act, Orders / Act, and % Tot Accts.
The report includes a Grand Total (Monetary) with accounts, revenue, orders, overall average revenue per account, average orders per account, and percentage of total accounts.
The Business Owner uses the report to determine whether the customer base is spending more or less and purchasing more or less often.

At step 1, if a full-fledged RFM analysis is required, the report is not intended to be a full-fledged RFM analysis, but rather give an idea of how the customer base is trending over time, and to tell us if they are spending more or less, purchasing more or less often, etc.
At step 3, if the Grand Total (Recency) percentage exceeds 100%, the report notes this is likely due to overlapping or cumulative categorization.
At step 4, if Frequency is 0, the report identifies the accounts as non-purchasing or inactive accounts.
